34/G.goal: Explain the Majuli Island virtual reality heritage preservation case study as a practical XR problem, from its main concerns and heritage-capture scope to the challenges of building an immersive interactive VR tour from its multimodal archive.
34/G.achieves: Provides the shared case-study context and problem definition needed to understand and implement an XR system with confidence in the later course lectures.

34/O1.goal: Characterize the main concerns and issues of the Majuli Island virtual reality heritage preservation and tour project.
34/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a shared understanding of the practical problem and user-experience constraints that later XR development work must address.

34/O2.goal: Describe how Majuli's tangible and intangible cultural heritage is organized into 24 hotspots for systematic heritage capture and documented as a multimodal heritage archive.
34/O2.achieves: Provides the concrete heritage-content and data model that later requirements, design, implementation, and optimization stages must handle.

34/O3.goal: Identify the key challenges in building an immersive interactive Majuli VR tour from the archival heritage information, including user requirements, design, usability testing, code testing, and cybersickness.
34/O3.achieves: Frames the specific XR development and user-experience problems that the remaining course lectures will address.
